No. The void second marriage means the couple could not hold as tenants by the entirety, so they most likely held as tenants in common, and the slayer rule only bars him from taking the decedent's share through her death. Her half passes to her estate, but he keeps his own undivided half, so the trial court's award of the whole property is probably wrong. Jurisdictions differ on how a defective marital deed is construed, which could change the exact split.
